desc:
When overlapping closed intervals [start, end] are merged (intervals that share at least one point, such as [1,4] and [4,5], are merged too), they form disjoint blocks. Number the blocks 0, 1, 2, ... from left to right.

The input list is in no particular order. For every interval of the input, in the given order, return the number of the block it ends up in.

intervals = [[8, 9], [1, 4], [4, 6], [2, 3], [6, 7], [20, 21]]
result    = [1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 2]

The blocks are [1,7] (made of four intervals), [8,9] and [20,21]. The interval [8,9] does not share a point with [6,7], so it forms its own block.
hints: Merging the intervals gives you the blocks, but sorting loses the original positions. What do you need to remember?
Sort the indices of the intervals by start instead of sorting the intervals themselves.

Sweep over the sorted indices with the usual merge rule. Keep the largest end of the current block; when an interval starts after it, increase the block counter. Write the current counter into result[index].
editorial: Sort the indices 0..n-1 by (start, end) and sweep. Maintain block (the number of the current block, starting at -1) and reach (the largest end in the current block). When the next interval's start is greater than reach (or there is no block yet), it opens a new block: increase block and set reach = end; otherwise update reach = max(reach, end). Store block in result[idx].

Because the sweep visits intervals in order of start, blocks are numbered from left to right automatically, and an interval can never join a block that was closed earlier. Time O(n log n) for the sort, O(n) space for the answer. Sorting a list of (start, end, index) triples is an equivalent way to carry the positions along.
solution:
def blockIndices(intervals):
    n = len(intervals)
    order = sorted(range(n), key=lambda i: intervals[i][0])
    res = [0] * n
    block = -1
    reach = -1
    for i in order:
        s, e = intervals[i]
        if block < 0 or s > reach:
            block += 1
            reach = e
        elif e > reach:
            reach = e
        res[i] = block
    return res
